notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-1-prob: Partition the2-by3rectangle into six unit squares. On a square[k,k+1]×[j,j+1], the floor is k+j on one half and k+j+1 on the other.
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-2-prob: Split at y=x. Symmetry gives2∫₀¹x e^(x²)dx=e−1.
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-4-prob: The vectors must be linearly independent. TransformE to the box[0,α]×[0,β]×[0,γ] and integrateuvw.
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-5-prob: Nonnegative geometric-series terms permit monotone convergence to the improper integral.
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-6-prob: Rotate the unit square using the stated map; integrate in u or v on the two triangular halves. The logarithm/trigonometric substitution evaluates the resulting improper integral toπ²/6.
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-7-prob: Expand the geometric series and integratex^k y^k z^k over the cube. For the alternating case, separate even terms or bound the alternating remainder.
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-8-prob: Differentiate arctan(tx) with respect tot and divide byx. The innerx integral isπ/(2t).
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-9-prob: Apply the chain rule twice using the coordinate maps; formulas apply away from coordinate singularities, with smooth extension interpreted in Cartesian coordinates.
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-10-pro: Horizontal force components cancel by symmetry. Integrate the vertical componentGmρd·2πr dr/(r²+d²)^(3/2), then letR→∞.
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-11-pro: Forfixedt the(y,z)regiont≤z≤y≤x is a triangle of area(x−t)²/2; continuity justifies reversing the integrals.
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-12-pro: Factor n from the square root; the remaining factor n^(−3) is the cell area(1/n)(1/n²).
notes.calculus-chapter-15-problems-plus-13-pro: Scalex=au,y=bv,z=cw to the unit ball. The cuttingplane has distance1/√3 from the center; integrate the capπ∫[1/√3,1](1−t²)dt and multiply byabc.
